status: sealed before measuring any trace distribution
honesty_notes: This is RETROSPECTIVE. The traces already exist and I hold literature priors about them (that single-GPU jobs dominate both Philly and Alibaba PAI). The seal records what I expect before measuring, but it cannot claim independence from prior knowledge, and this episode does NOT count toward real_prospective_cycle_count.

What my priors do NOT already answer is the DERIVED quantity: the largest scheduling-pool size at which whole-pool jobs are common enough to trigger the EP-0003 starvation mechanism. Nobody publishes that number. That is where this seal has teeth.

At the time of sealing I have downloaded pai_job_no_estimate_100K.csv and read only its column header, and I am downloading the Philly trace archive. No distribution, count, or summary statistic of either trace has been computed or viewed.

why_this_matters.claim_under_test: EP-0003 found that greedy size-priority scheduling starves the whole-pool job class once the need distribution's support contains N, at a rate as low as p=0.0005 of jobs. That result is about a synthetic model with N=64.
why_this_matters.the_stake: If real traces have NO jobs anywhere near pool size, or whole-pool jobs rarer than 0.0005, then the mechanism does not bind at realistic pool sizes and the practical implication in Current Understanding v3 must be WITHDRAWN, not merely qualified.
why_this_matters.pre_committed_consequence: If S2 and S4 both fail (neither trace reaches p>=0.0005 at any pool size >= 64), I will strike the v3 practical implications and record the mechanism as real but practically inert at cluster scale.

measurement_definitions.pai_gang_size: k = ceil(num_inst * num_gpu) over rows with num_gpu > 0. num_gpu < 1 denotes GPU sharing, so num_inst * num_gpu is the simultaneous GPU demand. CPU-only rows (num_gpu == 0) are excluded from the gang distribution and their share is reported separately.
measurement_definitions.philly_gang_size: k = number of GPUs held simultaneously by the job, taken from its longest/first successful attempt in cluster_job_log.json as the sum over that attempt's detail entries of len(gpus).
measurement_definitions.p_N: P(k >= N) over GPU jobs of that trace.
measurement_definitions.critical_pool_size: N* = the largest N in {8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048} with p_N >= 0.0005, the threshold measured in EP-0003. For any scheduling pool of size <= N*, whole-pool jobs arrive at least as often as the rate that produced starvation in E4.
measurement_definitions.work_share: share of sum(k * duration) carried by a job set, vs its share of job count.

predictions.claim: Alibaba PAI: single-GPU jobs (k=1) are at least 50% of GPU jobs
Alibaba PAI: a 64-GPU pool is already in the binding regime
predictions.confidence: genuinely uncertain -- PAI jobs are known to be small, and 64+ GPU jobs may well be rarer than 1 in 2000

predictions.claim: Alibaba PAI: the critical pool size is at least 128
Philly: the critical pool size is at least 128, i.e. any pool of 128 GPUs or fewer sees whole-pool jobs at or above the EP-0003 rate
predictions.confidence: moderate -- Philly is a training cluster with large multi-node jobs

predictions.claim: Powers of two dominate both traces, which is what makes ServerFilling applicable at all
predictions.criterion: in each trace, P(k is a power of two) >= 0.70

predictions.claim: Mean gang size is small in both traces
The large-gang class is rare by count but heavy by work, which is why a count-weighted view understates it
predictions.criterion: in each trace, (work share of jobs with k >= 64) / (count share of jobs with k >= 64) >= 10
predictions.falsified_if: the ratio is below 10 in either trace

predictions.claim: The real need distribution has a HEAVIER large-gang tail than my synthetic geometric family at the same mean, i.e. my theta family understated the danger
predictions.criterion: fit theta so that the geometric mix over (1,2,...,1024) has the same E[k] as the trace; then p_64(real) > p_64(geometric)
predictions.confidence: uncertain -- it could go either way

predictions.claim: The two traces agree on the critical pool size within a factor of 8
predictions.criterion: max(N*_pai, N*_philly) / min(N*_pai, N*_philly) <= 8, both defined
predictions.falsified_if: the ratio exceeds 8, or either N* is undefined

predictions.claim: Both traces contain jobs large enough to be whole-pool for a common pool size
predictions.criterion: max k >= 256 in Philly and max k >= 64 in Alibaba PAI

declared_unknowns: whether real clusters actually schedule over pools as small as N*, or always over the full cluster (the trace cannot answer this; it only says how often whole-pool jobs would appear at a given pool size)
whether the arrival process and duration correlation in the real trace change the starvation rate relative to the synthetic Poisson/exponential model
whether the Philly job log's GPU count reflects the gang requirement or only what was granted
the Alibaba v2023 openb trace caps num_gpu at 8 (node-level scheduling), so it cannot test the whole-pool question and is not used here
